scope: Foundry production sources including src/lib and diagnostic PageBench; exclude dependency/test/script/bench findings only

findings.description:
PageBench.readContiguous32FourPages() (src/PageBench.sol#46-53) performs a multiplication on the result of a division:
	- checksum += contiguous[(i / 8) * 128 + i % 8] (src/PageBench.sol#49)
findings.rationale: Diagnostic PageBench selects an integer page index: (i/8)*128 + i%8. This is intentional indexing, not financial arithmetic; PageBench is not deployed by Deploy.s.sol.

findings.description:
BatchAuction._place(address,uint8,uint16,uint64,bool) (src/BatchAuction.sol#178-208) uses a dangerous strict equality:
	- escrow > type()(uint128).max || meta.orderCount == type()(uint32).max (src/BatchAuction.sol#191)
findings.rationale: orderCount is checked against uint32.max before checked increment, starts at zero, and is decremented only for active cancellations. It cannot skip the sentinel. This equality prevents overflow; it does not test a manipulable token balance.

findings.description: BatchAuction._verify(AuctionTypes.Intent,bytes,uint8) (src/BatchAuction.sol#252-262) ignores return value by (signer,err,None) = ECDSA.tryRecover(keccak256(bytes)(abi.encodePacked(,DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(),hash)),sig) (src/BatchAuction.sol#257-258)
findings.rationale: ECDSA.tryRecover returns a diagnostic argument in its third result. The signer and RecoverError are checked and every failure becomes BadSig. Discarding only the diagnostic bytes32 does not accept an invalid signature.

findings.description:
Faucet.drip(address) (src/Faucet.sol#39-51) uses timestamp for comparisons
	Dangerous comparisons:
	- hasDripped[to] && block.timestamp < lastDrip[to] + 86400 (src/Faucet.sol#41)
findings.rationale: Intent expiration and the daily demo faucet cooldown intentionally use timestamps. Auction sealing uses block.number. Boundary tests cover deadlines/cooldown; neither timestamp comparison sets the clearing price.

findings.description:
BatchAuction._clear() (src/BatchAuction.sol#296-338) uses assembly
	- INLINE ASM (src/BatchAuction.sol#307-317)
	- INLINE ASM (src/BatchAuction.sol#326-336)
findings.rationale: The ladder copy is bounded to 256 ticks and reads only tagged entries. Result packing follows verified offsets and widths. Uncross assembly is separately reviewed; differential/permutation fuzzing and storage gates cover its memory and economic output. Slither cannot prove assembly correctness.

findings.description:
BatchAuction._place(address,uint8,uint16,uint64,bool) (src/BatchAuction.sol#178-208) has costly operations inside a loop:
	- askLots = _checkedAdd(askLots,lots) (src/BatchAuction.sol#199)
	Calls stack containing the loop:
		BatchAuction.placeMany(uint8[],uint16[],uint64[])
findings.rationale: placeMany must debit/store each order and update bounded uint64 side totals. Clients cap chunks at 50 through measured gas selectors; direct oversized calls revert atomically at gas limits. Clearing remains bounded to 256 ticks independently of order count.

findings.description: BatchAuction._place(address,uint8,uint16,uint64,bool) (src/BatchAuction.sol#178-208) has a high cyclomatic complexity (14).
findings.rationale: _place validates inputs, opens the batch, escrows and updates one of two ladders. This is covered by unit, overflow, differential and handler invariant tests; splitting it merely to reduce a style metric would risk measured bytecode changes.

findings.description: Variable BatchAuction.BASE (src/BatchAuction.sol#45) is not in mixedCase
findings.rationale: Uppercase immutable token/grid names and DOMAIN_SEPARATOR preserve the specified external API and familiar EIP-712 naming. This is a style finding.
